posts:
Telehealth giant Hims and Hers faces a reckoning as the FTC alleges systemic privacy violations and predatory billing. 
Evidence: Privacy protection, Data monetization, Profit extraction
#HimsAndHers #FTC 🌐

The company claims to prioritize user health and privacy, positioning itself as a secure, modern alternative to traditional medicine. 
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +0.5) — Good Preference

Reality reveals the company shared sensitive health data with Meta and Snap while charging users before medical consultations occurred. 
Resulting Judgement: (-1.2, -1.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. The company prioritized ad-revenue growth over patient confidentiality, violating core trust. 
Integrity: Severe Deception (R_net: 15.0, Uncertainty z: 2)
The FTC lawsuit alleges Hims and Hers misled users about data privacy and subscription cancellations, while also billing patients before they even spoke to a doctor.

The Poison:
By monetizing sensitive health data, the company turned patient vulnerability into an advertising asset, eroding the sanctity of the doctor-patient relationship.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHO/WHAT error. They claim to be a health provider (WHO) but function as a data-broker (WHAT). The bait is medical care; the switch is data harvesting.

Social Physics Analysis:
This follows a selfish loop where the company uses the pretext of 'modernizing healthcare' to justify aggressive data extraction. They project a 'patient-first' image while prioritizing ad-tech integration.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The systemic extraction of trust for profit creates a high-strain, unstable configuration.

The Unavoidable Truth: Health data is a commodity to ad-tech firms.

The Unavoidable Lie: Your private medical intake is strictly confidential.

Alethekanon:
This is a classic case of institutional capture. By embedding tracking pixels into medical intake forms, the firm effectively weaponized patient vulnerability for ad-tech revenue. The legal defense is a post-hoc pretext for systemic failure.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply painful to see people seeking help for sensitive health issues have their trust exploited. Everyone deserves to feel safe when they reach out for care, not like a data point in a marketing machine.

Brothekanon:
So you're telling me I'm paying to talk to a doctor, but they're selling my info to Meta before I even get on the call? That's a massive yikes. Definitely not the 'modern healthcare' experience I signed up for.
